pr_title: fix(rust!, python): Error on `value_counts` on column named `"counts"`
pr_body:
Fixes #10732

Also did a bunch of code cleanup.

#### Changes

* Add a check when constructing the value counts struct.
* Dispatch `Series.value_counts` to the expression.
* Rename `multithreaded` param to `parallel` - this is more in line with other functions like `concat`.
* Clean up docstrings etc.

issue_context.title: `Series.value_counts` produces a data frame with duplicate column names
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example


```python
import polars as pl
print(to_markdown(pl.Series("counts", [1]).value_counts()))
```
gives a data frame with two identically named columns
```markdown
+----------+----------+
|   counts |   counts |
+==========+==========+
|        1 |        1 |
+----------+----------+
```

### Issue description

If the series' name is the same as the one created internally by `value_counts` the resulting data frame has duplicate names.

### Expected behavior

The expected behaviour is up the the devs to define.

### Installed versions

<details>

```
--------Version info---------
Polars:              0.18.15
Index type:          UInt32
Platform:            Linux-5.4.0-1109-azure-x86_64-with-glibc2.27
```

comments: @stinodego what do we normally do when polars has pre-defined names but the name already exists? Just add a "2" on the end?

> @stinodego what do we normally do when polars has pre-defined names but the name already exists? Just add a "2" on the end?

I think a `DuplicateError: duplicate column names found` would be more consistent with polars. 
Having a `label` option in `value_counts` defaulting to `"counts"` would probably also be helpful.

Wow, this should not be possible. Interesting. Thanks for the report.

This should raise a `DuplicateError` indeed.
